subject: Request: detailed billing ledger + commit tiers for Q3
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@optifin.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwooding.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: detailed billing ledger + commit tiers for Q3

Hi Ava,

We are preparing the numbers for next quarter and need a line-by-line mapping between our invoices and token usage so Finance can reconcile with our internal chargeback model. Specifically: 
- A per-invoice CSV with daily token counts (prompt vs. completion) for the last 90 days
- A sample invoice line-item mapping that shows how Redwood aggregates tokens into line items (model, route, unit price, subtotal)
- Your recommended commit tiers for hosted API customers and the discount schedule by monthly token commitment (or annualized commit), plus any one-off rebate mechanics.

We need this to finalize the procurement request by end of month. Can you provide the ledger/export and a recommended commit proposal? Also include any assumptions about token counting for streaming responses vs. batch.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Director of Platform Engineering
OptiFin

---
Attachments: optifin_90d_token_ledger.csv (CSV stub)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwooding.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@optifin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwooding.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed billing ledger + commit tiers for Q3

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear ask. I attached an initial export (usage_export_May-Jun2026.csv) that breaks daily tokens into prompt/completion and tags the model and route.

A few quick notes and questions to make our commit recommendation accurate:
- Is the goal to set a monthly committed token slab for Q3 or an annualized commit with monthly drawdown?
- Do you want the recommended tier to assume predictable growth (+10%–20% m/m) or a flat baseline with burst capacity?
- Any constraints from Procurement on how discounts should appear on the invoice (e.g., line-item credit vs. net unit price)?

I'll draft a commit-tier proposal once you confirm those points. Cc'ing Karthik to prep the standard tier schedule and to flag any promotional flexibility.

Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: usage_export_May-Jun2026.csv (CSV stub)

From: Emma Li <emma@optifin.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwooding.com>
Cc: OptiFin Procurement <procurement@optifin.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T08:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed billing ledger + commit tiers for Q3

Hi Ava,

Thanks — the monthly committed slab is preferable for Procurement (they want discrete monthly budgeting). Please assume predictable growth of ~12% m/m. We prefer discounts to show as net unit price (simpler for our GL), but Procurement can accept a line-item credit if necessary — they'll weigh options.

Can you also provide: 
- A mapping that shows how each invoice line corresponds to tokens in the CSV (so we can reconcile quickly)
- A recommended 3-tier commit schedule for Q3 (conservative, expected, stretch) with corresponding unit price per 1k tokens and overall % discount vs list

Goal: present a single-page procurement justification and a reconciled ledger to Finance by Friday.

Emma

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwooding.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwooding.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwooding.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: detailed billing ledger + commit tiers for Q3

Internal — forwarding OptiFin's ask. They want: monthly commit slabs for Q3, per-invoice mapping to the token CSV, and a 3-tier recommended schedule. They prefer net unit pricing on the invoice.

Preliminary numbers from the export suggest a 3-month trailing average of ~650M tokens/mo with steady growth to ~730M if we apply the 12% m/m projection. Proposal options I think make sense: 
- Conservative: 700M/mo commit (12 months) -> 18% discount 
- Expected: 900M/mo commit (12 months) -> 25% discount
- Stretch: 1.2B/mo commit (12 months) -> 33% discount (requires finance/legal approval for promotional terms)

Karthik — can you prepare a clean pricing sheet (unit price per 1k tokens, invoice appearance examples) and flag which margins require approval?
Soojin — flagging for sign-off if we need >30% or non-standard rebate mechanics. We may also need the billing team to confirm how a net unit price vs. line-item credit will look in our billing export.

Thanks,
Ava

Attachments: pricing_schedule_Q3_v2.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwooding.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwooding.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwooding.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: detailed billing ledger + commit tiers for Q3

Thanks for the write-up, Ava. Approve a maximum promotional discount up to 28% for a 12-month commit at or above 2B tokens/month (this is a stretch guardrail but okay for strategic customers). For the bands below that: 18% (700M), 24% (900M). Anything above 28% needs CFO/legal review.

Please prepare: 
- A single-page procurement justification (I can sign) that includes the reconciled CSV mapping and the invoice example showing net unit price
- A short note for Legal describing the rebate logic if we pursue a line-item credit vs net unit price

Ava — you have sign-off to present the 3-tier sheet to OptiFin with the stated discounts; route final contract/redlines to Legal if OptiFin asks for >28% or non-standard credit terms.

Soojin Lee
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
